q-86684.name: Question 1
q-86684.problem:
Which of the following statements are logically equivalent?

I. $¬(¬X∧¬Y)$

II. $¬X∨¬Y$

III. $¬(X∧Y)$
q-86684.worked_solution:
Two statements are logically equivalent if they have the same truth table. So, we construct a truth table for the three given statements:

| $\,X\,$ | $\,Y\,$ | $\,¬(¬X∧¬Y)\,$ | $\,¬X∨¬Y\,$ | $\,¬(X∧Y)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

We see that only the statements $¬X∨¬Y$ and $¬(X∧Y)$ have the same truth table, so they are logically equivalent.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

q-182484.name: Question 3
q-182484.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬(¬P∨Q)\,$ | $\,P∧¬Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
¬(¬P∨Q){{field-4}}P∧¬Q
$$
q-182484.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P∧¬Q & ≡\text{T}∧¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}∧\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P∧¬Q & ≡\text{T}∧¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}∧\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(¬P∨Q) & ≡¬(¬\text{F}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬(\text{T}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬(¬P∨Q)\,$ | $\,P∧¬Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

To determine whether $¬(¬P∨Q)$ is logically equivalent to $P∧¬Q,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent. 

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{F},\text{T},\text{F},\text{F}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
¬(¬P∨Q)≡P∧¬Q.
$$

q-182496.problem:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∧¬B)\,$ | $\,¬A∨B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
¬(A∧¬B){{field-4}}¬A∨B
$$
q-182496.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(A∧¬B) & ≡¬(\text{T}∧¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬(\text{T}∧\text{F}) \\  & ≡¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬A∨B & ≡¬\text{T}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{F}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(A∧¬B) & ≡¬(\text{F}∧¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬(\text{F}∧\text{F}) \\  & ≡¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below. 

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∧¬B)\,$ | $\,¬A∨B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

To determine whether $¬(A∧¬B)$ is logically equivalent to $¬A∨B,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{T},\text{F},\text{T},\text{T}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
¬(A∧¬B)≡¬A∨B.
$$

q-182571.name: Question 5
q-182571.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬P∨¬(Q∨P)\,$ | $\,¬(P∧Q)∨¬P\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
¬P∨¬(Q∨P){{field-4}}¬(P∧Q)∨¬P
$$
q-182571.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∧Q)∨¬P & ≡¬(\text{T}∧\text{T})∨¬\text{T} \\  & ≡¬\text{T}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬P∨¬(Q∨P) & ≡¬\text{T}∨¬(\text{F}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∨¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∧Q)∨¬P & ≡¬(\text{F}∧\text{T})∨¬\text{F} \\  & ≡¬\text{F}∨\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}∨\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬P∨¬(Q∨P)\,$ | $\,¬(P∧Q)∨¬P\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

To determine whether $¬P∨¬(Q∨P)$ is logically equivalent to $¬(P∧Q)∨¬P,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they differ in the second row. Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
¬P∨¬(Q∨P)≢¬(P∧Q)∨¬P.
$$
